request.spec:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the policy versions viewer. Pressing "Show policy versions" now lists one line per version, oldest first, as `<version> <from or start> <key>=<value> <claims>`. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The database already stored every policy version, so no schema change was needed.

- **Server:** a new read-only endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/policy-versions`, in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/PolicyController.java`. It writes nothing to the store or the audit file. A version with no from-date shows `start`, and a value saved blank shows as `key=`.
- **Claim count:** for each version, this is how many of the sheet's claims show that number as their policy version (`claim-policy`). It uses the existing date rule, so the count always matches what each claim row shows.
- **Which claims count:** every claim on the sheet, including voided ones; scenario 3 needs a voided claim in the count. I didn't check whether deleted claims are listed, so they're counted too. Say if they should be left out.
- **Front end:** a small new component at `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/policy/policy.ts`, modelled on the existing Activity panel and placed just below it in `people.ts`. It has the `policy-show` button and the `policy-line` items, plus a `policy-error` message if the lines can't be loaded.
